Definition: akin to G4731; a "straining", "strenuousness" or "strength", i.e. (figuratively) luxury (voluptuousness):--delicacy.
BiblicalUsage: The word is luxury itself, the delicacies that made merchants rich. The merchants of the earth are waxed rich through the abundance of her delicacies, for all nations have drunk of the wine of her fornication.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the delicacies are the bait: the wealth of Babylon is built on the wine that makes nations drunk.
